slides.0.title: Grape varieties
slides.0.subtitle: GSM, Carignan, Cinsault and the whites
slides.1.title: The main reds
slides.1.highlights.0.title: GSM and C
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Grenache, Syrah, Mourvèdre, Carignan and Cinsault are the main reds, often blended as GSM or GSMC (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Division of roles
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Common shorthand: Grenache fruit and body, Syrah colour and spice, Mourvèdre structure, Carignan acidity and tannin, Cinsault light fruit (a style generalisation, not a rule)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: No single share
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The sources give no reliable area share per variety, so none is quoted
slides.1.content: Reds here are mostly blends, not single varieties.
slides.2.title: The Carignan story
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Aragonese origin
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Wine With Seth: almost certainly from Aragón in northeast Spain, named for Cariñena in Zaragoza province; also Mazuelo (Rioja), Samsó (Priorat), Carignano (Sardinia)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Late, high acid
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Late budding and very late ripening with naturally high acid and tannin; unchecked it can yield up to 200 hL/ha, so pruning and green harvest must control it (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Carbonic maceration
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Whole-bunch carbonic maceration is a defining Languedoc technique, softening tannins; Priorat and Roussillon more often destem and macerate longer (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.content: One variety, two faces, depending on yield and winemaking.
slides.3.title: Other reds
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Cinsault
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Used for rosé and light reds; the Languedoc AOC caps Cinsaut at 40% in reds (see lesson 4)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Grenache
slides.3.highlights.1.content: A principal variety of Languedoc AOC, alongside Lledoner Pelut, a Grenache relative
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Syrah and Mourvèdre
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The Languedoc AOC requires the two together to be at least 20% in reds (see lesson 4)
slides.3.content: The variety mix is actually written into appellation rules.
slides.4.title: Whites and others
slides.4.highlights.0.title: White varieties
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Piquepoul Blanc, Grenache Blanc, Roussanne, Marsanne, Vermentino, Clairette, Muscat, Bourboulenc and Viognier (Wine With Seth)
slides.4.highlights.1.title: The Limoux exception
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Limoux uses Chardonnay, Chenin Blanc and Mauzac (Wine With Seth)
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Pays d'Oc freedom
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Pays d'Oc IGP permits 58 varieties (Wine With Seth), which is why international varieties appear widely
slides.4.content: AOC leans on traditional varieties; IGP gives more freedom.
